title: Winter starry landscape
caption: The Milky Way over snow-covered trees, Torres del Paine National Park, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Snow-covered trees stand beneath a magnificent night sky in Torres del Paine National Park, in Southern Patagonia, Chile's XII Region. It is a long way from the desert observatories of the north, in a landscape of snow rather than sand. The two brightest stars in the prominent band of the Milky Way are Alpha Centauri, above, and Beta Centauri, below.

A little lower on the right sits the globular cluster Omega Centauri. On the left, above the trees, are the Small Magellanic Cloud and the globular cluster 47 Tucanae. A globular cluster is a dense ball of old stars held together by gravity.

Chile's desert skies are renowned for their clarity, but this picture shows that the rest of this long country can offer phenomenal stargazing too. Far to the south, snow and a clear night combine in a different kind of astronomical landscape.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph by G. Hüdepohl. The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: A camera can gather light for longer than the eye, so the star clusters and the Small Magellanic Cloud may look more distinct here than to someone among the trees.
